lines: +access: private          # only finance models may ref them (exceptions in _int__models.yml)
+      +persist_docs:          # write descriptions as COMMENTs in the warehouse
+ShopFlow is an online shop that sells in Morocco, Europe and the United States,
+* **Sources**: the app database (`shopflow_app`), the payment provider (`payments_provider`),
+  the website tracker (`web_analytics`) and the carriers (`shipping`).
+* All money in marts exists in the order currency **and** in EUR (monthly rates from the
+Current status of the order in the ShopFlow app.
+| pending   | the order is created, the payment is not confirmed    |
+| paid      | the payment succeeded, the parcel is not shipped yet |
+| shipped   | the carrier has the parcel                            |
+| delivered | the customer received the parcel                      |
+| cancelled | the order was cancelled before shipping (no revenue) |
+| returned  | the customer sent the parcel back and was refunded   |
+Amount converted to EUR with the exchange rate of the order month and currency
+(seed `exchange_rates`), rounded to 2 decimals with the `convert_to_eur` macro.
+Customer segment computed from the R (recency), F (frequency) and M (monetary) scores:

+-- concurrent_batches=false: DuckDB accepts only one writer at a time. With
+-- persist_docs (COMMENT ON after each batch) parallel batches hit
+-- "Catalog write-write conflict" errors, so the batches run one after the other.
-- Microbatch: dbt builds one batch per day and filters the upstream model
-- (which has event_time configured) to that day automatically. No is_incremental() needed.
